clue.text: Delegation which might make salesperson happy?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a diplomatic mission from one Commonwealth country to another
second, literal meaning: a big percentage paid on each sale

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase literally: commission is the cut a salesperson earns on a sale, so a lofty one would please them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Commonwealth country's embassy in another Commonwealth country is called its high commission, so the office and staff form a delegation.

clue.text: I urge showman to organise moving celebration

indicators.note: organising things puts them into a fresh order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone presses a showman to put on a stirring, emotional party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' looks like 'touching', but here it means relocating home.
explanation.definitionFit: A housewarming is the party thrown after moving into a new home, so it celebrates the move.

clue.text: Instrument maintaining current conditions at 13, say

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold and keep, so the instrument word holds the current symbol inside it

parts.note: a gong is a percussion instrument
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A device that keeps a steady flow running in some stated conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is ASCOT, a racecourse; the going is the state of the turf on a race day.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, the going describes how firm or soft the ground is at a course such as Ascot.

clue.text: Penning note, undercover journalist saw the light

indicators.note: penning something means enclosing it as in a pen, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: An undercover reporter, while writing a note, has a moment of revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: To see the light is an idiom for being won over to a belief, which is what a converted person has done.

clue.text: Game's poor player from the south on run round north

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a ham is a bad, over-the-top actor

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so the run word encloses the compass point

parts.note: to jog is to run gently
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A bad actor from the south of the country goes jogging round the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Player' suggests a game, but here it is an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese tile game for four players.

clue.text: I've tangled with darn unwelcome individual

indicators.note: things that get tangled end up in a jumbled order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone has quarrelled with a darning intruder, or simply been annoyed by one.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader enters a place where they are not wanted, so is an unwelcome intruder.

clue.text: Child artist, on the up, displaying sound technique

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the artist's letters run backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A young artist whose career is rising shows sound craftsmanship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar locates objects underwater by sending out sound pulses and hearing their echoes.

clue.text: Tell me where French nincompoop gets smacked

parts.note: to be smacked is to be hit

explanation.surface: Someone asks where in France a fool ended up getting slapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell me' reads as part of the question, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Out with it is an impatient spoken demand for someone to say what they are holding back.

clue.text: Trouble afoot, bishop going AWOL for wedding

indicators.note: someone AWOL is absent without leave, so the bishop's letter goes missing

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Trouble at a wedding as the officiating bishop goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is the union of two people in marriage.

clue.text: The poor, befuddled sot following Oasis

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the muddled drink word is placed second, after the refuge word

parts.note: an oasis is a refuge, a haven

indicators.note: a befuddled person is confused, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard; taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor folk and a confused drunk trail after the band Oasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oasis' could be the Manchester band, but here it is just a safe place.
explanation.definitionFit: The have-nots are those who lack money or possessions, the poor as a social group.

clue.text: Riot guards owning manscaping product

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a riot, something hilarious, is a scream

explanation.surface: Riot police protect their own grooming products.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riot' looks like civil disorder, but it means something very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Manscaping is men's grooming of body hair, and shaving cream is used to remove it.

clue.text: Composer overlooking a novelist and painter

indicators.note: to overlook something is to miss it out, so that letter is dropped from the composer

explanation.surface: An artist list: a composer, a novelist and a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: El Greco was the Cretan-born painter who worked in Toledo, Spain.

clue.text: Frenzied dancer very embarrassed-looking about his pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged into a poor order
about can mean turned around, so the preceding pair is read backwards

explanation.surface: A wild dancer goes red with embarrassment over his trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English pants means underpants and also rubbish, so it serves as an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirling dervish is a Sufi devotee who spins in an ecstatic dance.

clue.text: Character twice in arena — national sports venue

parts.note: the only letter appearing twice in the word arena
a Scot is a national of Scotland

explanation.surface: A national sports arena is described by some letter that appears in it twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Daily help for refs welcomed by ones producing match-day serenade

indicators.note: someone welcomed by others is taken in among them, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: a char, or daily, is a cleaning lady
one is I; the plural word supplies two of them, either side
VAR, the video assistant referee, helps football officials

explanation.surface: Football talk: a cleaner plus video replays for referees produce a chant on match day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like football, but it means a marriage; a charivari is a mock serenade of banging pans for newly-weds.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade given to a newly married couple, so a wedding-day serenade.

clue.text: Reformer grabbed by Schoenberg or Bach even

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside the grip of the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of Schoenberg, all of or and Bach, and the start of even

explanation.surface: A reformer is seized by Schoenberg, or even Bach.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Gorbachev reformed the Soviet Union with perestroika and glasnost.

clue.text: A doctor, filled with rage, upset container for drink

indicators.note: something filled with other things holds them inside
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

explanation.surface: A furious doctor knocks over the cup holding a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An Americano is a coffee made by adding hot water to espresso.

clue.text: Republican admitted to hateful action and didn't go straight

indicators.note: someone admitted to a place is let inside it

explanation.surface: A Republican confesses to a nasty act and admits he was not on the level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Didn't go straight' suggests crime, but it means a winding course.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander along a winding route, not following a straight line.

clue.text: Said why drunk seaman turns up in shabby fashion

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from the bottom, so the sequence runs backwards
said tells us to use the letter that sounds the same as the following word

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like why

explanation.surface: Someone asks why a drunken sailor appears so scruffy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty can mean shabby or worn, so rattily is the adverb for doing something in a shabby way.

clue.text: Parent defends platform for provocative movement

indicators.note: a defender stands around what it protects, so the parent wraps the platform

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a dais is a raised platform

explanation.surface: A parent stands up for a platform promoting provocative activism.
explanation.definitionFit: Dadaism was an early twentieth-century art movement that set out to shock and provoke.

clue.text: In a declamation contest, school scoffed

indicators.note: declamation is speaking aloud, so we want a word that sounds like the school

parts.note: Eton is the English public school near Windsor

explanation.surface: A school's pupils scoffed at a public-speaking competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed' seems to mean mocked, but it means wolfed down.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is British slang for gobbling it, so scoffed food has been eaten.

clue.text: Having the least art, a composer books tours

indicators.note: to tour something is to go all the way round it, so the books enclose the rest

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a set of books

explanation.surface: A composer with the least artistic skill takes books on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' here is guile or cunning, not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless or unsophisticated, so the naivest person has the least guile.

clue.text: Heartless, evil as well as horny bounder

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its middle letter

explanation.surface: A cruel, lecherous cad is described as heartless and evil.
explanation.walkthrough: Evil has four letters, so its heart is the middle pair; a bounder is British slang for a cad, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns, and antelopes leap, so it is a horned jumper.

clue.text: Like some faith in side playing with a lot of credit

indicators.note: playing about with the letters moves them into a new order
a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A sports side plays on heavy credit, which says something about their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene, so deistic describes that kind of faith.

clue.text: One in a powerful suit back in hot seat

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the rump is the backside, what one sits on

explanation.surface: A powerful figure is back in the hot seat, with a nod to the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a trump is any card of the suit that outranks the others.

clue.text: Great Italian player, one lacking belief in Picaroon

parts.note: a pagan is a non-believer in the main religions
Picaroon is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: A great Italian player has no faith in the setter Picaroon.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian virtuoso violinist.

clue.text: Crack up first in Amsterdam, with drug problem returning

indicators.note: first in a word means its opening letter only
returning means going back, so the drug and problem are read backwards

parts.note: a sum is a maths problem

explanation.surface: Someone cracks up in Amsterdam when their drug problem comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks drug-related given the surface, but crack up means make laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack someone up is an idiom for making them laugh, which is to amuse them.

clue.text: Tipsy trio of Englishmen missing soft sound of music

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk

indicators.note: something missing is absent, so the letter for soft is taken away

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an Englishman, three times
p, piano, means soft in music

explanation.surface: A drunken threesome of Englishmen miss a quiet bit of The Sound of Music.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the film title The Sound of Music; tiddly-om-pom-pom imitates a brass band's oompah.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly-om-pom-pom is a nonsense phrase imitating the jaunty rhythm of a band, so a musical sound.
